methodology.sampling_strategy: Stratified: 17 COGNITIVELEVEL_UPDATE (Packs A/B/C/D, all 6 sections), 18 BOTH_UPDATE (Pack E, all 6 sections). For 23 items, full choice set extracted to verify same-domain distractor pattern.
verification_sources: Direct stem extraction from pack files via PowerShell regex
Choice set extraction confirming same-domain distractor pattern (Agent D, Agent E findings cross-referenced)
Agent E boundary analysis decision rules
Agent D Pack E per-section analysis

findings: All 168 COGNITIVELEVEL_UPDATE items (Evaluate@Easy → Understand@ME/2) follow the identical template pattern: '[Company] [scenario]. Which response is most appropriate?' — confirmed across Pack A (120+ items, Sections A-F), Pack B (3 items), Pack C (6 items), Pack D (3 items). Template artifact is the root cause, not per-item mislabeling.

All 76 BOTH_UPDATE items (Difficult@Remember → Understand@ME/2) are Pack E items with definition-recall format. Agent D's per-section analysis (Section A: 32 should-be-Understand, B: 40, C: 50, D: 44, E: 63, F: 55 = 284 total) encompasses this 76-item subset. Agent E's boundary analysis confirms same-domain distractor pattern as the root cause of Remember→Understand drift.
All 244 items converge on a single output: CognitiveLevel=Understand, Difficulty=Moderate-Easy, DifficultyScore=2. This is DCS §3 compliant (Understand default is ME/2).

No pack exhibits different treatment for items in the same category. Pack E items get BOTH_UPDATE because both CL AND Difficulty are miscalibrated (Remember+Difficult) vs. Pack A items where only CL is wrong (Evaluate+Easy, difficulty is already close to correct). The difference is driven by starting conditions, not methodology inconsistency.

phase_1_calibration_check.details: All 244 proposed new pairs (Understand, Moderate-Easy/2) are DCS §3 compliant. Understand→ME/2 is the DCS default. The same-domain distractor pattern (confirmed in 23 choice-set verifications) supports ME/2 rather than Easy/1 — the candidate must discriminate between plausible concepts within the same domain, which is characteristic of Understand-level comprehension.

phase_2_rubric_adherence.details: CAQS v1.0 §6.2 defines Understand as 'explain concepts, interpret meaning.' Agent C's decision consistently identifies items where the cognitive demand is comprehension of a single GAAP/standard/budgeting concept with discrimination between same-domain alternatives. The Evaluate→Understand downgrade is justified because none of the 168 items exhibit genuine evaluative judgment (multiple defensible answers, trade-off between frameworks, professional judgment under uncertainty). The Remember→Understand upgrade (Pack E) is justified because same-domain distractors require concept comprehension, not mere recall.

phase_3_evaluate_to_understand_audit.verdict: PASS — all 168 items are template artifacts, not genuine evaluation
phase_3_evaluate_to_understand_audit.confirmed_pattern: ALL 20 sampled stems follow '[Company] [specific-GAAP/COSO/budgeting-context]. Which response is most appropriate?' Each item tests comprehension of a single correct treatment under a specific standard. No item presents competing frameworks requiring professional judgment.
true_evaluate_characteristics_absent: No items with multiple defensible answers
No items requiring trade-off between competing standards
No items with IMA ethical dilemma requiring principle prioritization
No items where 'which response is most appropriate?' genuinely means 'which of these defensible approaches is BEST' versus 'which is the GAAP-correct treatment'

verified_samples.stem: Umbra sells equipment with a separately priced installation service that is distinct from the equipment. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: ASC 606 performance obligation recognition. Single correct treatment. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Delta learns after year-end that a major customer was bankrupt at year-end. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Subsequent event classification. Single correct GAAP treatment. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Harbor sold inventory to its subsidiary and the inventory remains unsold to outsiders at year-end. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Intercompany elimination. Single correct consolidation treatment. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Orion is classifying a three-month Treasury bill purchased near maturity. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Cash equivalent classification. Single correct treatment. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Summit uses executive-imposed targets with little manager input. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Top-down budgeting identification. Concept comprehension. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Willow wants budgeted resource needs tied to expected activities. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Activity-based budgeting identification. Concept comprehension. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Crescent observes a consistent upward pattern in monthly demand. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Time-series trend component identification. Concept comprehension. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Umbra evaluates a department manager. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Responsibility accounting concept. CC=C: 'Assess costs and revenues the manager can significantly influence.' Single correct principle. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Evergreen worries ROI discourages managers from accepting profitable projects above the required return but below current ROI. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: ROI disincentive → RI solution comprehension. CC=B: 'Use residual income to reduce the incentive to reject value-adding investments.' Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Harbor uses cheaper material that creates excessive scrap. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Variance analysis: material price vs. material usage variance identification. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Umbra produces a homogeneous chemical in a continuous process. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Process costing identification from business characteristics. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Crescent allocates service costs only to production departments. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Direct method of service department allocation. Single correct identification. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Juniper tests units before shipment. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Appraisal cost (COQ framework) identification. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Beacon receives an invoice from a vendor for raw materials that Beacon never ordered and never received. Which control would have most effectively prevented payment on this fraudulent invoice?
verified_samples.verdict: Internal control application to fraud scenario. Tests understanding of control-type-to-risk mapping. Understand is correct; borderline Apply but clearly not Evaluate.

verified_samples.stem: Northstar is reviewing internal controls related to shipping document prenumbering. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: Control activity classification (prenumbering = completeness control). Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Quartz is building a model to label transactions as high-risk or low-risk based on known examples from prior reviews. Which analytics method best fits this use case?
verified_samples.verdict: Analytics method identification. CC=B: Classification. Choices: A=Clustering, C=Regression, D=Outlier detection — ALL analytics methods from same domain. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Evergreen is evaluating least privilege access in a finance transformation project. Which response is most appropriate?
verified_samples.verdict: IT access control principle comprehension. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: The sales department of Pinnacle Products is evaluated based on total sales revenue generated... This department is best classified as:
verified_samples.verdict: Responsibility center classification (revenue center). Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Elderberry's production supervisor is evaluated only on the costs incurred in the department, with no control over revenue or investment decisions. What type of responsibility center is this?
verified_samples.verdict: Cost center classification. Definition-match with context. Understand.

verified_samples.stem: Thornbury decides to purchase insurance to address a significant identified risk rather than eliminate the underlying activity. What enterprise risk management response is this?
verified_samples.verdict: ERM risk response identification (risk sharing/transfer). Understand.

phase_4_edge_cases.verdict: PASS — no decisions found to be incorrect

borderline_items.note: Could be Apply rather than Understand (scenario-specific control selection). Agent C classified as Understand. Given that the item tests comprehension of which control maps to which fraud type (not executing a multi-step procedure), Understand is acceptable. The distinction from Evaluate (original CL) is clear — there is one correct control answer, not genuine evaluative judgment.

phase_4_pack_e_duplicate_stems.finding: P1E-A-007 and P1E-A-008 both extract with stem 'Under U.S. GAAP, goodwill is:' but their choices differ (A-007 CC=B=annual impairment test; A-008 CC=A=purchase of equipment, suggesting A-008 is actually a different question about investing cash flows). Possible stem extraction artifact (DL-016 metadata-block shift) or actual content duplication. Either way, this does NOT affect the BOTH_UPDATE metadata decision — both items are currently Remember/Difficult and correctly downgraded to Understand/ME-2.
phase_4_pack_e_duplicate_stems.severity: Informational — no impact on metadata review

governance.dl016_concern: NOTE: For Pack A/C/D items with dual-block architecture (metadata block + content block), Agent C's plan only modifies the metadata-block CognitiveLevel/Difficulty/DifficultyScore. The content block may have independently stored values that differ (per DL-016 finding). The execution phase should verify that BOTH blocks are updated to maintain consistency. This is an implementation concern, not a decision error — the CL assignment is correct; the implementation must ensure both blocks receive the update.

execution_recommendations: Batch the 244 items in ≤30-item groups per governance-guard Rule 5
Backup each pack file before modification per BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md
For dual-block packs (A/C/D): update CognitiveLevel/Difficulty/DifficultyScore in BOTH the metadata block and the content block to resolve DL-016 divergence
For Pack B/E items (single-block): direct field update is sufficient
Run DCS §3 compliance scan post-modification to verify zero new misalignments
Re-run 'Select-String -Path pack_*_corrected.js -Pattern "question_state.*Certified"' to confirm certified pool count unchanged (no question_state modifications)
